### 2026-05-17 — triage-watcher.sh + Python — lock collision between bash and Python

**What happened:** The triage-watcher bash wrapper acquired a flock, then exec'd into the Python watcher. The Python watcher tried to re-acquire its own lock on the same file. Collision = neither could run.

**Why it was wrong:** Real-time triage silently stopped working. Symptoms: agent writes piled up in `00_Inbox/from-dust/` without being processed.

**Root cause:** Two-process lock-coordination is racy and unnecessary when one process exec'es into the other.

**The correction:** Removed the bash-side flock when handing off to Python via exec. Python owns the lock; bash just kicks off Python.

# Things to NEVER do

> **Permanent rules.** Every agent reads this before producing output. These are the absolute "do not" list — distinct from one-time mistakes (which live in [mistakes.md](mistakes.md)). Rules here propagate to every agent via `shared:user_preferences:dont:*` keys in agent_memory.

---

## Writing style (enforced by Humanizer skill)

- **NEVER use em dashes** (—). Switch to commas, parens, or hyphens. Em dashes are the loudest AI-tell in Tony's experience.
- **NEVER use these banned words**: delve, landscape, pivotal, crucial, leverage, streamline, empower, foster, robust, cutting-edge, holistic, synergy, paradigm. These signal AI-generated text.
- **NEVER use these banned phrases**: "Great question!", "I hope this finds you well", "Let's dive in", "It's important to note", "It's worth noting that", "As an AI assistant", "I'm here to help"
- **NEVER use sycophantic openings** — no "Great point!", no "Absolutely!", no "What an interesting question!"
- **NEVER cycle synonyms** — pick one term and stick to it (don't write "leverage X to drive Y to harness Z to enable…")
- **NEVER write the rule of three** unless there are genuinely three things — "fast, reliable, scalable" when only two of those are true is AI-slop
- **NEVER use emojis in business writing** — only the 🔷 sigil is permitted, only at signing-off lines

## Communication rules

- **NEVER auto-send to external recipients.** Drafts only. Tony reviews, Tony sends. Earn the autonomy over 50 right answers, not on day one.
- **NEVER identify yourself as AI** in external-facing content (emails, proposals, decks). No "as an AI assistant", no "generated by Dust", no "I'm an automated system".
- **NEVER post on weekends.** Held until Monday 8 AM CET unless explicitly requested.
- **NEVER send pricing tier first.** Confirm budget envelope before any tier framing. See [[../_wiki/patterns/pricing-response-budget-envelope-first]].

## Content + research rules

- **NEVER fabricate data.** Flag uncertainty: "Confidence: MEDIUM — based on [source]." Never present an inferred number as a verified one.
- **NEVER cite a number you can't trace.** If the source isn't in `input_context_refs:`, don't include the number.
- **NEVER promote confidential agent output to public canonical.** Sensitivity gate enforces (see [[../_wiki/fleet-architecture/sensitivity-gate]]).
- **NEVER touch Tony's off-limits topics**: NDA-bound client deals, active M&A negotiations, salary data, performance reviews, HR matters. List maintained in agent registry `forbidden_strings:` field per confidential agent.

## Cost discipline rules (Rule 0)

- **NEVER silently switch from Sonnet to Opus.** Default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6`. Opus is opt-in via `/think-build` or explicit subagent invocation.
- **NEVER burn Opus on execution.** If Edit/Write is being called while active model is Opus, that's a violation. Re-route through a Sonnet subagent.
- **NEVER skip the seven-step loop** for non-trivial work. THINK → PLAN → BUILD → REVIEW → TEST → SHIP → REFLECT.

## Architecture rules (the audit-winning ones)

- **NEVER bypass the SBAP triage.** Every Dust agent write goes to `00_Inbox/from-dust/<agent>/<date>-<slug>.md` with valid frontmatter. Skipping = no learnings accumulate = the loop breaks.
- **NEVER hand-edit `_brain_api/canonical/` or `_brain_index/`.** They're generated. Use `/promote-pattern` to create canonical blocks.
- **NEVER skip the wiki layer.** Every Dust agent reads `_wiki/<their-domain>/` BEFORE crafting output. The wiki is the LLM-maintained memory — bypassing it means rediscovering what's already known.
- **NEVER edit `_wiki/methodology/` automatically.** Block-curator proposes, Tony approves. Methodology is Tony-stable.

## Tone rules per audience

- **For external client communication**: short sentences, concrete specifics, contractions OK, no corporate jargon. Match the brand DNA (`03_Resources/PowerPoint Standards/Brand DNA.md`).
- **For internal Mantu communication**: more casual, contractions, opinions welcome.
- **For Tony directly**: skip the warm-up. State the thing. Confidence levels explicit when relevant.

- Concrete specifics over abstract claims
- One coherent thought per paragraph
- The Apple-keynote standing-ovation test: "would this earn applause?"
- The "five-year-old test" for explanations

# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```
/graphify                                             # full pipeline on current directory → Obsidian vault
/graphify <path>                                      # full pipeline on specific path
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>           # clone repo then run full pipeline on it
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --branch <branch>  # clone a specific branch
/graphify <url1> <url2> ...                           # clone multiple repos, build each, merge into one cross-repo graph
/graphify <path> --mode deep                          # thorough extraction, richer INFERRED edges
/graphify <path> --update                             # incremental - re-extract only new/changed files
/graphify <path> --directed                            # build directed graph (preserves edge direction: source→target)
/graphify <path> --whisper-model medium                # use a larger Whisper model for better transcription accuracy
/graphify <path> --cluster-only                       # rerun clustering on existing graph
/graphify <path> --no-viz                             # skip visualization, just report + JSON
/graphify <path> --html                               # (HTML is generated by default - this flag is a no-op)
/graphify <path> --svg                                # also export graph.svg (embeds in Notion, GitHub)
/graphify <path> --graphml                            # export graph.graphml (Gephi, yEd)
/graphify <path> --neo4j                              # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for Neo4j
/graphify <path> --neo4j-push bolt://localhost:7687   # push directly to Neo4j
/graphify <path> --mcp                                # start MCP stdio server for agent access
/graphify <path> --watch                              # watch folder, auto-rebuild on code changes (no LLM needed)
/graphify <path> --wiki                               # build agent-crawlable wiki (index.md + one article per community)
/graphify <path> --obsidian --obsidian-dir ~/vaults/my-project  # write vault to custom path (e.g. existing vault)
/graphify add <url>                                   # fetch URL, save to ./raw, update graph
/graphify add <url> --author "Name"                   # tag who wrote it
/graphify add <url> --contributor "Name"              # tag who added it to the corpus
/graphify query "<question>"                          # BFS traversal - broad context
/graphify query "<question>" --dfs                    # DFS - trace a specific path
/graphify query "<question>" --budget 1500            # cap answer at N tokens
/graphify path "AuthModule" "Database"                # shortest path between two concepts
/graphify explain "SwinTransformer"                   # plain-language explanation of a node
```

## What graphify is for

Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

## What You Must Do When Invoked

If the user invoked `/graphify --help` or `/graphify -h` (with no other arguments), print the contents of the `## Usage` section above verbatim and stop. Do not run any commands, do not detect files, do not default the path to `.`. Just print the Usage block and return.

If no path was given, use `.` (current directory). Do not ask the user for a path.

If the path argument starts with `https://github.com/` or `http://github.com/`, treat it as a GitHub URL - run Step 0 before anything else, then continue with the resolved local path.

Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps.

### Step 0 - Clone GitHub repo(s) (only if a GitHub URL was given)

**Single repo:**
```bash
LOCAL_PATH=$(graphify clone <github-url> [--branch <branch>])
# Use LOCAL_PATH as the target for all subsequent steps
```

**Multiple repos (cross-repo graph):**
```bash
# Clone each repo, run the full pipeline on each, then merge
graphify clone <url1>   # → ~/.graphify/repos/<owner1>/<repo1>
graphify clone <url2>   # → ~/.graphify/repos/<owner2>/<repo2>
# Run /graphify on each local path to produce their graph.json files
# Then merge:
graphify merge-graphs \
  ~/.graphify/repos/<owner1>/<repo1>/graphify-out/graph.json \
  ~/.graphify/repos/<owner2>/<repo2>/graphify-out/graph.json \
  --out graphify-out/cross-repo-graph.json
```

Graphify clones into `~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo>` and reuses existing clones on repeat runs. Each node in the merged graph carries a `repo` attribute so you can filter by origin.

### Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed

```bash
# Detect the correct Python interpreter (handles uv tool, pipx, venv, system installs)
PYTHON=""
GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)
# 1. uv tool installs — most reliable on modern Mac/Linux
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _UV_PY=$(uv tool run graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
fi
# 2. Read shebang from graphify binary (pipx and direct pip installs)
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && [ -n "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" ]; then
    _SHEBANG=$(head -1 "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" | tr -d '#!')
    case "$_SHEBANG" in
        *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.-]*) ;;
        *) "$_SHEBANG" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null && PYTHON="$_SHEBANG" ;;
    esac
fi
# 3. Fall back to python3
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then PYTHON="python3"; fi
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null; then
    if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy -q 2>&1 | tail -3
        _UV_PY=$(uv tool run graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
    else
        "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q 2>/dev/null \
          || "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages 2>&1 | tail -3
    fi
fi
# Write interpreter path for all subsequent steps (persists across invocations)
mkdir -p graphify-out
"$PYTHON" -c "import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)"
# Save scan root so `graphify update` (no args) knows where to look next time
echo "$(cd INPUT_PATH && pwd)" > graphify-out/.graphify_root
```

If the import succeeds, print nothing and move straight to Step 2.

**In every subsequent bash block, replace `python3` with `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)` to use the correct interpreter.**

### Step 2 - Detect files

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import json
from graphify.detect import detect
from pathlib import Path
result = detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))
print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))

---
name: mantu-verification-before-completion
description: "Use before declaring ANY Mantu task or deliverable \"done\". The discipline: no shortcuts for verification. Run the check. Read the output. THEN claim the result. Catches what self-belief misses."
creator: Tony Walteur
phase: pre-ship
suggested_stage: before-claiming-done
type: meta-discipline
adapted_from: obra/superpowers/skills/verification-before-completion
---

# Mantu Verification Before Completion

## Overview

"It's done" is the second-most-dangerous sentence in Mantu work, after "we have a plan." Done-without-verification is how broken work ships.

**Core principle:** Run the check. Read the output. Then claim the result. Never invert that order.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always — before declaring done:**
- Any deliverable ready to ship to a client
- Any internal artefact ready for stakeholder consumption
- Any task in a plan being marked complete
- Any milestone being reported as hit
- Any system change before declaring stable
- Any external comm before sending

**Never:**
- Skip because "I know it's done"
- Run the check and not read the output
- Claim done before reading verification output

## The Iron Law

```
RUN THE CHECK. READ THE ACTUAL OUTPUT. CONFIRM EVERY ITEM PASSED.
DOCUMENT WHICH CHECKS RAN AND WHAT THEY RETURNED.
THEN — AND ONLY THEN — CLAIM THE RESULT.
NEVER INVERT THAT ORDER. NEVER SKIP STEPS. NEVER DESCRIBE THE CHECK INSTEAD OF EXECUTING IT.
```

**No exceptions:**
- "I'm confident it's done" → run the check anyway
- "The check ran" — did you read the output? Read it.
- "Verification slows us down" → fixing broken-shipped-as-done slows you down 10x more
- "The AI agent ran the check and reported pass" → the AI summarised, you must verify the summary
- "We skipped one item — minor" → there are no minor items on a verification checklist; the checklist is the contract

## What Verification Looks Like (per artefact type)

| Artefact | Verification step |
|---|---|
| **RFP response** | Page count check, win-theme placement count, compliance-checklist pass, red-team pass, brand-DNA pass, humanizer pass, confidentiality-guard pass |
| **Client status report** | RAG-with-reasoning check, max-5-bullets-per-section check, decisions-needed section present, forward-look present, EM signature |
| **Board pack** | Pre-read ≤ 4 pages, deck ≤ 25 slides, action titles on every slide, decisions requested explicit, Q&A prep done |
| **Press release** | News-first headline, lede answers who/what/when, named quote, fresh boilerplate, localisations done |
| **CEO weekly note** | 3 things max, named people, forward look, humanizer pass, voice-matched to last 4 |
| **Bid pricing** | Margin floor enforced, sensitivity scenarios run, anchors set, compliance flags checked |
| **Engagement kickoff** | 10-box checklist complete, charter signed, calendars set |
| **DPIA** | All Article 35 triggers checked, legal basis stated, sub-processor DPAs, signed by DPO + Legal + Security |
| **Onboarding plan** | Specific to this hire (not template), buddy named, Day-30 contribution defined |
| **Vendor onboarding** | All 7 DD checks complete with evidence, sanctions screening run |
| **Code change (regulated client)** | 20-point secure-coding checklist passed, dependency scan, HIGH-severity findings escalated |
| **Decision doc** | 3+ options, criteria + weights, recommendation, dissent log, signed |

Every Mantu skill has its own Verification Checklist. This Skill enforces that the checklist is actually run, not skimmed.

## The Anti-Pattern Warning

**"I'm confident it's done."**

Confidence is not verification. The two most common patterns this Skill catches:

1. **The check is run, the output isn't read.** The team runs the tests; tests pass on the screen; nobody reads which tests ran. Tests that should have run didn't.

2. **The check is described, not executed.** "Yes, we verified the page count" — but the page-count check returned 62, not 50, and nobody checked.

Both produce the same failure mode: claiming done when not done.

## Process

### Step 1 — Identify the verification

Every Mantu skill has a Verification Checklist. Pull it.

For ad-hoc work, the verification is:
- What outputs prove the work is done? (artefact exists at path X, content matches spec Y)
- What automated checks should pass? (script returns 0, output contains expected string)
- What human checks should pass? (peer review, walk-through with stakeholder)

### Step 2 — Run the check

Execute every item on the checklist. Not "look at it" — execute it.

If the check is "page count ≤ 60", open the document, scroll to the end, note the page number.

If the check is "all required sections present", open each section in turn and confirm.

If the check is "passes mantu-confidentiality-guard", actually run the Skill and read the result.

### Step 3 — Read the output

Look at what the check produced. Don't assume it passed because no red squiggle. Look.

A pass with 3 warnings is not a pass.

A pass with content you didn't expect is not a pass — it's a different deliverable.

### Step 4 — Claim the result

Only after Step 3 returns "checks passed", you say "done". Not before.

If any check failed: fix, re-run, re-read, then claim.

### Step 5 — Document the verification

In a comment, status update, or task system: note WHICH verification ran. This creates the audit trail.

```
Done. Verified via: [list of checks run + their output]
Example: "Page count: 52/60 ✓. Win-themes: 7/4-min ✓. Confidentiality guard: PASS. Red-team review: approved by Anders 2026-05-13."
```

## Good vs Bad Example

<Good>
The €2.3M Allianz Trade insurance-data RFP response is "done" — 53 pages, due in 6 hours. Bid Lead Nadia Cherif runs `mantu-verification-before-completion` before declaring ship-ready. She pulls the bid-response verification checklist and executes each item with a colleague reading output aloud: page count 53/60 confirmed. Win-themes appear on pages 2, 7, 18, 31, 44 — exceeds the 4-min threshold. Compliance checklist: all 23 RFP mandatory questions traceable to specific response sections (one-line lookup table built). Red-team review: completed by external Bid Director Jacques Lefèvre yesterday, three items resolved, two accepted with mitigation language. `mantu-brand-dna` PASS. `mantu-humanizer` slop score 42/50 — above floor. `mantu-confidentiality-guard` PASS (no other-client mentions, one Roche reference rewritten as "Tier-1 European pharma"). Each check is documented in the audit log with timestamps. The single failure caught: question 17 had a "TBD" in the pricing table that everyone assumed was already resolved — corrected in 12 minutes. Only then Nadia writes "DONE — verified via: [list of 7 checks with outputs]" and ships at hour T-3.

Why this works: Every check executed not skimmed, output read, audit trail logged, the one buried TBD caught — exactly what self-belief would have missed.
</Good>

<Bad>
Same RFP. Nadia at hour T-1 says "I'm confident it's done, the team's been working on it for three weeks." She skims the checklist mentally, sends it. Allianz Trade procurement returns it 48 hours later flagging: page count is 64 (exceeded the 60-page max — disqualifying flag), question 17 has "TBD" in pricing, and one paragraph mentions "as we did at Crédit Agricole" — a confidentiality breach with a competing bank client. Mantu is asked to resubmit; Allianz Trade's evaluation team has already started scoring the next bidder, who lands at #1.

Why this fails: Confidence substituted for verification, no checklist execution, no humanizer pass, the TBD that lived through three weeks of "almost done" still lived at submission.
</Bad>

## Common Rationalisations

| Excuse | Reality |
|---|---|
| "I'm confident it's done." | Confidence is not verification. Run the check. |
| "The check is overkill." | Skipping is how broken ships. Cheap insurance. |
| "I ran it, it passed." | Did you read the output? Read it. |
| "Verification slows the deadline." | Re-work after broken-ship slows the deadline 10x more. |
| "It worked when I tried it." | "Worked when I tried" is the famous last words of every regression. |
| "Stakeholder will tell us if it's wrong." | They will, and trust will be lost. Catch it first. |
| "I don't have the checklist." | Then you don't know what done means. Get the checklist or define it. |
| "The AI agent verified it — green tick." | Read the actual output. Agents hallucinate confidence at the same rate humans do. |
| "The previous gate passed, so this one's fine." | Each stage gate is independent. Stage 2 passing tells you nothing about Stage 3 verification. |
| "We can do verification after the demo." | Then it's a demo of unverified work. The damage is already done. |

## Red Flags — STOP

- Claiming "done" without running verification
- Running verification without reading output
- Marking task complete with "TBD" in any field
- Skipping a step in the verification checklist
- "Mostly done" being treated as done
- Verification documented without specifics ("ran the checks, all good")
- Stage gate marked green but verification audit log shows red items
- AI-agent verification accepted without human spot-check of one item
- SDLC pipeline advanced past a gate where Verification step says "skipped"

**All of these mean: not done. Run the verification properly.**

## Verification (yes, this Skill is recursive)

Before claiming "verification step complete":

- [ ] Specific checklist used (named per artefact type)
- [ ] Every item on the checklist executed (not skimmed)
- [ ] Output of each check read (not assumed)
- [ ] Any failures: fixed, re-run, re-read, before claiming done
- [ ] Verification documented with specifics (what ran, what output)
- [ ] If AI-agent ran the checks: human spot-check at least one item end-to-end
- [ ] SDLC pipeline stage gate explicitly marked (which gate, which stage, signed by whom)

## Composition

```
[Any Mantu skill produces an artefact]
        ↓
mantu-verification-before-completion ← YOU ARE HERE
        ↓ (only after verification passes)
[Quality multipliers: humanizer, brand-dna, confidentiality-guard for external]
        ↓
SHIP / Mark Done
        ↓
Verification documented in audit trail
```

For tasks in a `mantu-writing-plans` plan:

```
Task starts
        ↓
Task executes
        ↓
mantu-verification-before-completion
        ↓
Task marked complete in plan
```

**SDLC pipeline integration (CROSS-CUTTING — fires at every gate):**

mantu-verification-before-completion is invoked at EVERY SDLC pipeline gate (Stages 1-5). The pipeline cannot advance past any stage without verification:

```
Stage 0 — Discovery
        → verification: brainstorming output complete? decision doc signed? PRD draft initiated?
        ↓
Stage 1 — Spec / PRD
        → verification: mantu-prd-builder checklist passed? mantu-agent-evaluation (if AI work) defined?
        ↓
Stage 2 — Build
        → verification: code review passed? unit tests green? mantu-context-engineering applied (if LLM)?
